drivers.lead: Rea equalled Carl Fogarty's four in 2018, passed it at Magny-Cours in 2019 and finished on six, every one of them consecutive
drivers.note: Six in a row, 2015 to 2020, all with Kawasaki, and no other rider has won more than four. Fogarty's four came in two pairs, 1994 and 1995 then 1998 and 1999, and stood as the record for nineteen years. Rea beat it with two rounds to spare in 2019 and added a sixth the following season at Estoril. He retired from full-time racing at the end of 2025 after two years with Yamaha. What makes the number hard to approach is who is left to try: Toprak Razgatlıoğlu and Troy Bayliss are the only other riders on three, and Razgatlıoğlu — champion in 2021, 2024 and 2025 — moved to MotoGP for 2026. Álvaro Bautista, in 2022 and 2023, is the only other rider of the last decade with more than one. Beating six would mean winning six championships from a standing start.

teams.lead: Ducati has won 21 of the 38 manufacturers' titles awarded since the championship began in 1988, and has led outright since 1994
teams.note: Honda took the first three, in 1988, 1989 and 1990, and has not led since. The run that built Ducati's record is really two runs: six straight from 1991 to 1996, then seven straight from 1998 to 2004, with 1997 going to Honda in between. After 2011 came a decade without one, while Aprilia and then Kawasaki took over, and Ducati has since won four in a row from 2022. The last two of those are the strange ones, because Ducati took the manufacturers' championship in 2024 and 2025 while Toprak Razgatlıoğlu won the riders' title on a BMW in both years — depth across several competitive riders outscoring one dominant bike. Kawasaki is second on seven and would need fourteen more to draw level, which is more than any manufacturer other than Ducati has won in the whole history of the championship.
